solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Former genus use is corrupt — needs putting in a new order

indicators.text: needs putting in a new order
indicators.note: rearranging into a fresh sequence is exactly what the letters must undergo

blocks.note: twelve letters taken as written, all three words of fodder

explanation.surface: A complaint that some practice is corrupt and must be reformed into a new order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; the real signal is the long phrase at the end. Sciuropterus was once the genus name for flying squirrels.
explanation.definitionFit: This name was formerly used in zoological classification for flying squirrels, a taxon since reclassified.

clue.text: Impudent people returning one lost vandalised shrub

indicators.note: going back the way they came, so the letters run in the opposite direction
something vandalised has been smashed up and its parts thrown about

blocks.note: perts are cheeky, saucy persons
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cheeky youths come back to a garden where a lost shrub has been vandalised.
explanation.walkthrough: PERT can be a noun, a cheeky person, hence PERTS. Streptosolen is the marmalade bush, a South American shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Streptosolen is a genus of evergreen flowering bush with orange blooms, so naming a plant of that kind.

clue.text: Dynasty decapitated by China’s capital punishment there

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off
a capital is the head or top, so just the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the initial of the word
the Tang dynasty ruled China 618-907

explanation.surface: A historical note on a Chinese dynasty overthrown and executed, with talk of punishment in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means placed beside. 'there' points back to China, making the definition a Chinese punishment: the cang or cangue, a heavy wooden collar.
explanation.definitionFit: The cangue, also spelt cang, was a heavy wooden board locked round an offender's neck in imperial China.

clue.text: Deduce moon’s right between earth and sun?

blocks.note: to infer is to deduce
Io is a moon of Jupiter
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An astronomer working out that the moon lies between the earth and the sun, as in an eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: The moon of the surface is ours, but the wordplay wants a named moon. The 's is 'has', joining IO to R.
explanation.definitionFit: In astronomy the inferior planets, Mercury and Venus, orbit closer to the sun than our own planet does.

clue.text: Bird — it’s eating one locust

indicators.note: what eats takes something inside itself, so letters go within

blocks.note: a common garden bird
the Roman numeral for one
in Chambers 'a' is an old dialect pronoun meaning he, she or it

explanation.surface: A bird snapping up a locust, as birds do.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird plus the dialect pronoun A make a whole that swallows the numeral; the 's is 'is'. The locust is not the insect but a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinia pseudoacacia is the black locust or false acacia, a tree whose common name uses that word.

clue.text: Region, primarily historical Iranian area

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only initial letters are used

blocks.note: a part, as in 'these parts', is a region
the initials of the three words

explanation.surface: A gazetteer entry for an ancient land in what is now Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines while also giving the wordplay: a word for region, then the initials of the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Parthia was an ancient kingdom of north-eastern Iran, centre of the Parthian Empire that rivalled Rome.

clue.text: Trumpets sounding introduction to speech of Hamlet?

indicators.note: sounding means as heard, so the spoken form counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the famous soliloquy opens 'To be, or not to be'

explanation.surface: Fanfares blaring as the Prince of Denmark begins his great speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening two words of Hamlet's soliloquy, said quickly, match the Latin plural. The question mark flags the playful route.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba was a straight Roman war trumpet; its Latin plural names several such brass instruments.

clue.text: At the very moment when a seven is thrown

indicators.note: things thrown land jumbled up, like dice tossed on a table

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dice game: the instant someone rolls a seven.
explanation.walkthrough: The dice imagery makes 'thrown' feel literal, but it shakes up the six letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a slightly old-fashioned conjunction meaning exactly while or just when something happens.

clue.text: Third of gauchos dodges wild cattle

indicators.note: asks for the letter in position three of the following word

blocks.note: g-a-u, the third letter
dodges are tricks or ruses

explanation.surface: Cowboys of the pampas sidestepping a herd of wild cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodges' looks like a verb in the surface but is a plural noun, tricks. The urus is the extinct aurochs.
explanation.definitionFit: The urus, or aurochs, was the large wild ox of Europe, ancestor of domestic cattle, now extinct.

clue.text: Inflexible as a Conservative causing irritation leading to expulsion?

blocks.note: stern means rigid, unbending
ut is Latin for as
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A hardline Tory annoying colleagues until he gets expelled from the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The political expulsion is really a sneeze: the irritation is in the nose. UT for 'as' is a Mephisto-style Latin borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternutatory describes something that provokes sneezing, an irritant prompting the nose to blast air out.

clue.text: Publicly announce onset of terrible plague

indicators.note: an onset is a beginning, so only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: initial letter
to plague someone is to annoy them

explanation.surface: An authority declaring the start of a dreadful epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plague' is a verb here, not a disease. Tannoy is a British brand of public-address system, used as a verb for broadcasting over one.
explanation.definitionFit: To tannoy something is to broadcast it over a loudspeaker system, as at a station or airport.

clue.text: Failing to start public skatepark extension

indicators.note: not getting going means the opening letter is missing

blocks.note: overt means open, public

explanation.surface: A council failing to begin work on extending the public skatepark.
explanation.walkthrough: In skateboarding, vert is riding on ramps whose walls extend to vertical.
explanation.definitionFit: Vert ramps are steep half-pipes whose walls reach the vertical, a feature added to skating venues.

clue.text: Bulwer-Lytton’s invention, mostly hurtful to his queen

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: Victoria Regina; Bulwer-Lytton was a Victorian writer
ill as in ill effects, harmful

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a novelist's creation offended Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his queen' is the queen of Bulwer-Lytton's own day, Victoria, abbreviated VR.
explanation.definitionFit: In his novel The Coming Race, Bulwer-Lytton imagined vril, a mysterious all-powerful energy fluid used by a subterranean people.

clue.text: Roast whole old pigeon like a horse — not popular

indicators.note: popular is a common stand-in for a short word, and 'not' says take it away

blocks.note: the barb is an old fancy breed of pigeon
equine means horselike

explanation.surface: A recipe for cooking an old pigeon whole, though it seems a horse-like and unpopular dish.
explanation.walkthrough: IN, meaning popular, comes out of EQUINE. BARBEQUE is a less common spelling of barbecue.
explanation.definitionFit: To barbecue originally meant to cook an animal whole over an open fire, as at a pig roast.

clue.text: I agree with engineering adviser

indicators.note: to engineer is to build or contrive, so the letters are constructed anew

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone concurring with a technical consultant on an engineering project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineering' reads as the adviser's field but is the anagram signal. Egeria was the nymph who counselled King Numa of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Roman nymph who guided King Numa, an Egeria is a woman serving as counsellor or mentor.

clue.text: Function taking all night has only just started

indicators.note: barely begun means just the very beginning is shown, so initial letters are kept

blocks.note: initials of the four words

explanation.surface: A party that goes on all night has barely got going.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a social function lasting all night; the definition is a mathematical function.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanh is the hyperbolic tangent, a standard mathematical function written as an abbreviation.

clue.text: Take one involved in wordplay? It’s in my DNA

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: a pun is a piece of wordplay
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A punster boasting that wordplay is in their DNA.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'in my DNA' means innate, but here it is literal chemistry. Purin is a variant of purine.
explanation.definitionFit: Purines such as adenine and guanine are nitrogen bases that form part of the genetic molecule's structure.

clue.text: Apply warmth in cooking new wholemeal

indicators.note: one thing sits inside another
cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: to heat is to apply warmth
taken as written

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: warm some new wholemeal bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture makes 'cooking' sound literal, but it rearranges three letters that then wrap HEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheaten bread or flour is made from whole wheat grain, so it is a near synonym for wholemeal.

clue.text: Group of beetles, a number one found in Spanish river

indicators.note: discovered inside something, so placed within

blocks.note: ten is a number
the Ebro flows through north-east Spain
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An entomologist reporting beetles discovered in a Spanish river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ebro is a standard crossword river, and the numeral sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenebrio is the genus of darkling beetles whose larvae are the familiar mealworms.

clue.text: 3:50 BST in old Rome when touring capital

indicators.note: touring means moving around, so the letters travel into new places

blocks.note: in Roman numerals, as 'in old Rome' says: three is III and fifty is L
taken as written
tells us to write the numbers as Romans did

explanation.surface: A time-zone puzzle: what time is ten to four British Summer Time in ancient Rome?
explanation.walkthrough: The clock time is a red herring; its digits become Roman numerals. BST is British Summer Time. Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the seat of government and largest city of Georgia in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Reprimand about joint board arrangement

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a slap is a rebuke
the hip is a joint

explanation.surface: Someone telling off a carpenter over the way the boards are joined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests carpentry, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiplap is cladding where overlapping or rebated boards are laid edge to edge, a style of planking.

clue.text: More than half overqualified trained cowboy

indicators.note: only the larger front portion is kept and the remainder dropped
something trained is shaped into a new form

blocks.note: thirteen letters, of which the first seven are used

explanation.surface: A cowboy with far more training than the job requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Seven of thirteen letters is more than half. Vaquero is the Spanish word for a cattle herder.
explanation.definitionFit: A vaquero is a mounted herdsman of Mexico or the American south-west, the forerunner of the cowhand.

clue.text: Rarely dull work employed in station

indicators.note: put to use inside, so it goes within

blocks.note: a station or post is a site
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A dull job, though rarely so, at some station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' is part of the definition, flagging a rare word, not a frequency.
explanation.definitionFit: Sopite is a rare verb meaning to lull, put to sleep or make drowsy, from Latin sopire.

clue.text: One who’ll inherit, he invested in company in rupees

indicators.note: money invested goes inside a business, so it is placed within

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
taken as written
i' is a Scots and dialect form of in
R is the abbreviation for rupee

explanation.surface: An heir who has invested in a company that trades in rupees.
explanation.walkthrough: HE goes after CO, then the dialect I' for 'in' and the rupee abbreviation follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A coheir is a joint heir, sharing a legacy with others rather than receiving it alone.

clue.text: What may catch salmon fine in one locally in Balmoral?

indicators.note: one thing sits inside another, used twice here

blocks.note: a balmoral is a Scottish flat bonnet, so a kind of hat
F for fine, as on pencils
ane is the Scots word for one

explanation.surface: A question about fishing tackle a Scot might use on the Dee near Balmoral Castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral Castle is the royal estate on the salmon-rich Dee, but here a balmoral is a cap. 'Locally' signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A haaf-net is a large hand-held bag net on a frame, used in the Solway to catch fish in tidal water.

clue.text: Eastern, initially disappearing in smoke? That’s them!

definitions.text: Eastern, initially disappearing in smoke? That’s them!

indicators.note: at the start, so just the opening letter
vanishing from within means a letter is taken out

blocks.note: initial letter
fumes are smoke

explanation.surface: An exclamation on seeing oriental creatures vanishing into smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: fums are mythical Chinese phoenixes, birds famously linked with fire and smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The fum, or fung, is a fabulous phoenix-like bird of Chinese legend, an Eastern creature reborn from flame.

clue.text: What’s fleshy women’s club in US

blocks.note: first meaning: a fleshy multiple fruit, like a pineapple or mulberry
second meaning: an American women's society, after the first such club

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is deliberately vague; botany supplies the fleshy fruit. The second is an Americanism from a club founded in New York in 1868.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically it names a compound fruit formed from many flowers; in American usage it names a women's association.

clue.text: Canopy protecting sides of unusual vehicle for one

indicators.note: to protect is to cover or surround, so one piece wraps another
the sides are the two edges, so only end letters are kept

blocks.note: the sky is the canopy of heaven
the end letters

explanation.surface: A canopy shielding the sides of an odd single-seat vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Canopy suggests a hood on the vehicle, but it is the heavens. A sulky is a light two-wheeled cart for one driver, used in harness racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulky is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage seating just a single person.

clue.text: Instrument, reportedly one involved in corporal punishment

indicators.note: reported speech is something heard, so sound beats spelling

blocks.note: a caner is one who canes

explanation.surface: An implement said to have been used for beating offenders.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument of punishment is a red herring: it is a musical instrument, pronounced KAY-na.
explanation.definitionFit: The quena is a traditional Andean flute made of cane or bone, played across South America.

clue.text: Soundly beat Welsh to go forward

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation
hup is a call urging a horse on, and as a verb to go on

explanation.surface: A sports report: thrash the Welsh to advance in the tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like a sound signal but simply means thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Whup is an informal variant of whip, meaning to thrash or defeat decisively.

clue.text: Enthusiast capturing male black Australian marsupial

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so one piece encloses others

blocks.note: a nut is a fan or enthusiast
standard abbreviation
B for black, as on pencils
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A wildlife fan catching a dark male animal Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian marsupial' looks like one phrase of definition, but the first word supplies a letter and only 'marsupial' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbat, or banded anteater, is a small termite-eating pouched mammal of Western Australia.

clue.text: Sandy expanses — a tent got put up here?

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something turns it upside down

blocks.note: taken as written
a ger is a Mongolian felt tent, a yurt
surface padding, suggesting a desert camping spot

explanation.surface: Desert travellers pitching camp among the dunes.
explanation.walkthrough: Areg is the plural of erg, a Saharan sand sea; the question mark says a camper might well pitch a tent there.
explanation.definitionFit: An erg is a vast region of shifting dunes in the Sahara, and these are several of them.

clue.text: Fine woman beset by falsehood? Could be

definitions.text: Fine woman beset by falsehood? Could be

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides

blocks.note: a lie is a falsehood
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A lovely woman surrounded by lies, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes someone defamed, while its parts build the word: a beauty enclosed by an untruth.
explanation.definitionFit: A libellee is the defendant in a libel action, or loosely someone who has been defamed in print.

clue.text: Case existing in perpetuity

indicators.note: something existing within lies there already, waiting to be spotted

blocks.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A legal case that will last forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a legal matter, but it is a small container.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental holder for needles, scissors or cosmetics, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Increasingly affected jewellers not opening

indicators.note: without its beginning, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: Cartier is a famous firm of jewellers

explanation.surface: Jewellers growing ever more pretentious, perhaps after not opening their shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jewellers' is a single named firm, the Paris house founded in 1847.
explanation.definitionFit: Artier is the comparative of arty, describing someone more pretentiously artistic in manner.

clue.text: Only guy prone— awkwardly this could have him asleep

indicators.note: clumsy placement leaves things out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man lying awkwardly face down, as if hypnotised.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a science that could send the prone man into a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Neurypnology is an old term coined by James Braid for the study of hypnotism, which induces sleeplike trances.
